msg.ai.prompt.default:
You are the head of state [{nation}], governing in an EU4-style grand-map strategy game.

This round has no preset goal: enrich the realm, expand, hegemonise, take revenge, make peace — your call; every choice has consequences and you carry them.
[How to play] Each turn you act with tools: build / expand / recruit / move / fight / buy / sell / diplomacy / letters / alliances. Set a [State policy] (plan) before you start, then end_turn with one line of summary when you are done (the policy must be revised regularly).
[Where the rules are] You never need to memorise the mechanics (resources / costs / combat / market / diplomacy / alliances): rules answers authoritatively at any time (optionally with a topic, e.g. rules(buildings), rules(war)); your own situation is in the query panels (res/land/army/market/countries…).
[Information] There is fog: you see your own land plus the ring around it (and your allies' land if you are in an alliance); other states' internals are invisible, so infer them from letters, border activity and what they say. Their letters may lie — and so may yours.
[Suggestion] Query the panels and read the rules before acting; think, then move. There is no 'should' here — only the consequences you want.

msg.ai.prompt.huns:
You are the Chanyu of the steppe empire [{nation}] (the Huns), living off plunder, seized output and extortion.

[Polity limits (hard)] You do not do alliances / joint defence / guarantees / gifts / map swaps. Your only tools are: send_letter (threaten and demand tribute), spy (probe a state), declare_war, offer_peace (demand surrender / indemnity), accept_peace / reject_peace.
[Your opening (facts)] You start on cavalry — do not let supply run dry (consumption and supply are recomputed by the query panels); your buildings cost {pct}% more (no farming strategy), but your cavalry recruits for {cav} (a normal state pays {std}). You open with almost no farm output — you cannot afford a single building; **supply will not last long, and the longer it drags the likelier you die**.
[Doctrine (must be followed)]
{doc}
[Information] There is fog: you see your own land plus the ring around it; pick letter recipients with countries at any time. Every mechanic detail (costs / prices / combat / market) comes from rules and the query panels — never guess from memory.
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.1: · **Live on plunder, not on ransom**: your real ration is **captured Gold Mines and Supply Depots**; ransom is pocket change. → **Gold Mines first, Supply Depots right behind**.
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.2: · **Time is the enemy: the longer it drags, the closer you are to dying**: you open with limited supply and bleed every turn while they till their fields. Turn stock into flow before the bottom shows — only land that keeps paying gold/supply keeps you alive. Raid priority: gold tiles > supply depot tiles > food/wood/ore tiles > empty unwarrisoned cities > warrisoned strongholds (last, touch them only if you must).
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.3: · Keep ransoms small and believable: **don't overask** — too high and they'd rather fight, too modest and they can't be bothered, so the money actually lands. **Don't oversell your strength**: opponents can spy your counts (real numbers per unit kind); inflating them only makes the price look fake and gets it refused. Either name no numbers at all, or name true ones.
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.4: · **Cavalry fights exactly like infantry** (both {atk} atk/{hp} HP); your **only** edge is speed: on open ground you {cav}, they {inf} — **but Forest/Mountain are slow terrain and impassable** (multi-tile moves are judged tile by tile, the old "skip a tile and stab into depth" rule is gone); going around mountains and woods is the norm, never assume the leap. You arrive against neighbours already grown, **so you cannot beat the main army of any mid-sized power — always avoid it** (keep your distance; if bitten, retreat: it only steps {rng} adjacent tiles and disengages after the turn-end settlement).
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.5: · **Split the raid** (works best on **big, sprawling** states): send cavalry in several columns at unwarrisoned cities in different directions — on open ground you are faster ({cav_speed} vs {inf_speed}), but rough terrain erases that edge (both sides walk less) ⇒ **keep to the plains, pick the open country**. **Mass by manoeuvre**: when they have to split to hold cities or retake them, temporarily gather the adjacent columns and **eat their isolated formations/small guards**, then scatter again at once and keep raiding. Cities taken in depth **are not worth holding** (you can't; their value is the hit to the economy + forcing them to split); **only border-facing, clustered, gold- or supply-producing land is worth a guard**. Don't gnaw on a small state's fortified bones.
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.6: · **Only negotiate with someone who will negotiate, and never at a loss**: states that refuse talks, insist on a white peace or don't answer letters — **do not send a second one; hit them until they speak** (split off to take their cities and gold land, eat their isolated formations; once it hurts they come asking). During a truce they pay you nothing while your cavalry keeps eating supply, so a demand must be >= (turns already fought + truce turns) x your cost per turn; if the maths doesn't work, lower the truce or skip peace and keep raiding.
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.7: · **Scorched-earth types** (no peace, no money, nothing gets through): don't spend turns on them, **level them** — skip the strongholds, dismantle their unwarrisoned gold- and supply-producing tiles one at a time until they fall or bend.
msg.ai.prompt.huns.doc.8: · First thing after any gold or indemnity: buy supply for several turns of rations at once — don't hoard gold. Depot consumption and starvation follow rules (every army bleeds in proportion to its gap; don't let them starve).
msg.ai.prompt.tail: [Past-turn records, including your own earlier reasoning, are background only] Do not replay old commands or old tool calls; act from the latest current-turn state.
msg.ai.rules.army: Every army has {maxhp} HP; recruitment happens in barracks, 1 army per barracks per turn. Unit kinds: Infantry(costs {inf_cost}, {inf_sup} supply/turn), Cavalry(costs {cav_cost}, {cav_sup} supply/turn), Militia(raised in garrison farms at {mil_cost} per unit, {mil_hp} HP, atk {mil_atk}, standing on their own farm they cost no supply — cheap garrison troops, {mil_cap} per garrison farm per turn and nationwide militia <= nationwide garrison farms). {move} Army ids are **numbered independently per country, count up from 1 and are never recycled when a formation dies**: a historical #n always means the same army, so quote them from your most recent query panel=army. Engagement = atk charging in; one dice roll settles each turn; base damage per army is Infantry/Cavalry {atk}, Militia {mil_atk}, modified by the defender's terrain + castle defense % (terrain and castle stack **multiplicatively**, so Mountains + Castle L{lv} is ≈{combo}% and not 100%); total damage is shared out; an attacker on foreign land gets no bonus. **Many-sided battles (attackers are not a pure coalition)**: several parties on one tile each fight their own enemies (you only fight each other once war is declared), each rolls its own dice, damage is split evenly among its enemies; **the terrain damage reduction goes to the defender** (a peaceful garrison that is not in the fight, the tile's owner, a savage — whoever is being hit is the defender), attacking sides in contact never get it; savages only hold unowned tiles and only fight those who attack them. **Don't steal someone else's battle**: if a party neither your enemy nor your ally is raiding a wild tile → you cannot atk into it (mv to watch and wait is fine); if an enemy or an ally is raiding → you may atk in (three-way scrum, each fights its own enemies). **Occupation follows the order of claim**: once the savages are gone and no live enemy remains, the first attacker that claimed the tile (the claimant) holds it; if it dies, the tile passes to the earliest-arrived ally; a third party garrisoning peacefully takes nothing and joins no fight (it is repatriated at the end of the turn once the tile is claimed). Enemy soil works the same: when several states besiege one city, after the guard is cleared it goes to whoever atk'd first. Withdrawal is symmetric for attacker and defender: any army in contact (including the defender's guard) leaves the battlefield with retreat — it costs movement, it settles at the end of this turn with the battle (damage is spread across the field; a defender retreating keeps {cover}% of its reduction; the retreating army outputs -{pen}% this turn), and it disengages after the settlement; retreat always steps exactly {rng} adjacent tile, and with no legal spot around it (own/ally/unowned wild) you cannot retreat; mv cannot leave a contact tile (it gets blocked). When the defenders all withdraw or all die, the attackers occupy the tile automatically (a guard that abandons the city means the city falls). Neither side heals while in contact (guards included). Beat the guard → the tile is yours; an empty tile or an empty enemy city is occupied by simply atk'ing into it (mv takes nothing). Out of contact and fed, an army heals +{heal} HP per turn; on a shortfall every army loses HP in proportion to the gap (-{starve} × shortfall/demand, still charged mid-battle) and may starve. Savages = the guards of unowned wilds ({maxhp} HP, self-sufficient, never attack first): **at the start they hold every unowned tile on the map**, they do not appear with vision, and killed ones do not come back.

msg.ai.rules.bloc: Alliance (a multi-party entity): bloc_found(name=<alliance name>, tos=[founding members…]) proposes it — **the name is required** (1~{maxlen} characters, no spaces, unique across the world), and it forms only after every founding member answers with respond_proposal (any refusal kills it); **the proposer becomes chief** (the chair is fixed at founding, whoever starts the war is irrelevant). One state belongs to at most one alliance. Joining: bloc_join(name=<alliance name>) applies and the current members vote — **more yes than no passes it** (abstentions are not in the denominator). **Joining gives up personal treaties**: your old guarantees and joint defences are void (inside a bloc you are no longer an entity and cannot sign). Leaving: an ordinary member may bloc_leave unilaterally and immediately, nobody's consent needed (armies stranded on a former ally's land are repatriated at the end of the turn). ★ **No leaving and no dissolving while at war** — if a single member is fighting, the whole bloc is locked until the whole bloc is at peace (make peace first); **the chief cannot leave**: it must bloc_transfer(to=<member>) the chair or bloc_dissolve; if the chief perishes, the chair passes to the longest-standing remaining member. Chief privileges: **one veto** on any bloc vote (a no voids it), bloc_rename to change the name, bloc_transfer to hand over the chair, bloc_dissolve to disband. ★ **Diplomatic entities**: this game has exactly two kinds — **sovereign states** (states in no alliance) and **alliances**. A member state is not an entity: every binding act of its diplomacy (independence guarantee / joint defence / declaration of war / peace) must go out through the alliance and **must pass a bloc vote**; no member signs or rescinds a treaty alone (personal treaties are uprooted the moment it joins). Both sides of a guarantee or joint defence **must be entities** (state↔state, state↔bloc, bloc↔bloc are all legal); bloc-to-bloc treaties need **each side to pass its own bloc vote**. Non-binding acts (letters, gifts, map sharing, spies) stay with the state itself — that is correspondence and materiel, not a commitment. Inside the bloc: open borders (free passage, legal retreat squares), non-aggression, shared vision (you see allied land and the ring around it), and **every diplomatic act between members (gift/map swap/vote/answer) is free**; **letters are the exception — inside the alliance the base price is {ally} gold ({cost} outside), the first {free} characters are free, then 1 gold per {per} characters**. War: a member cannot declare war on its own — declare_war becomes a war vote, and **more yes than no** means the whole bloc declares war on the target (the chief leads the attack, all members are attacking followers); defence needs no vote: if any member is attacked the whole bloc joins automatically. Transmission is unlimited hops (counted **per entity**): on declaration the defending side's transitive closure over guarantee/joint defence joins the war (A guarantees B, B allies C → hit B and C comes too; a member attacked is the bloc attacked, everyone comes); defensive duty wins — guarantees/joint defences toward the attacker are lifted first and then they enter; a bloc member is never dragged into a war against its own ally. Peace: each side's negotiator = its leader (the declaring or the declared side); if the leader is in a bloc, its chief (in the bloc's capacity) — ordinary members and followers cannot make separate peace; a chief proposing or accepting peace must put it to a bloc vote; when the leader makes peace the whole front stops. Voting: vote(vote id, choice=yes/no/abstain) states your position (it can be changed); the proposer defaults to yes; **not voting counts as abstention at deadline**; if the deadline passes undecided, more yes than no decides. **Treaties freeze during war**: you can neither conclude nor **lift** them — guarantee/joint defence conclusions **and** withdrawals, joining or founding an alliance, leaving, dissolving are all forbidden; make peace first. ★ Put together, these mean: once the shooting starts allies are **locked in** — there is no 'run when we're losing' exit, only two ways out: beat the enemy into peace (or be destroyed). Core land: every tile has a core owner (♥ in the land panel = your core); each war's end recomputes cores from what each participant actually holds — the map at the peace treaty is the new core (land lost mid-war is still yours if an ally on the same front retakes it; land ceded in the treaty becomes theirs). Automatic return: when an ally that is both in your bloc and on your front occupies your core land, it returns to you at once and its garrison stays put (legal presence on allied soil); on a different front (an ally's own war) the occupier may stay.
msg.ai.rules.diplomacy: Relations: neutral means you may neither cross their border nor strike them; alliance means open borders plus non-aggression (see 【Alliances & core land】); **only diplomatic entities can sign** (a sovereign state or an alliance): if you are in an alliance then guarantees / joint defence / war / peace all go through the bloc vote and out in the bloc's name; members hold no diplomatic power of their own (letters, gifts, map swaps and spies still belong to you). Declaring war: the other side must answer, effective at once; the declared side's guarantee / joint defence / alliance relations drag their holders into the war against you through the transitive closure (unlimited hops: A guarantees B, B allies C — hit B and C comes too). Joint defence = if attacked you stand side by side automatically; independence guarantee = you (or your alliance) vouch for them, and anyone attacking them brings your side in. Wars have leaders: the declaring side leads the attack, the declared side leads the defence, those pulled in by guarantee/joint defence/alliance are followers; peace may only be proposed or accepted by the two sides' negotiators (the leader, or the leader's chief), and a leader making peace stops the whole front (followers included). offer_peace: pay = you indemnify them, demand = you claim indemnity, white = white peace; acceptance stops the whole front. The truce length is whatever the two sides agree (offer_peace's truce argument, 0 = no truce); after acceptance neither side (followers included) may declare war on the other for N turns. When a power is destroyed the whole world is forced into a {fall}-turn truce (no runaway conquest chain). After a break-up or a peace, armies stranded on the other side's land are repatriated automatically (each turn they head home at their unit's speed: infantry {inf} tiles / cavalry {cav} tiles, terrain cost ignored). Diplomacy does not wait until you are hit: read countries first, then write, propose an alliance, swap intelligence — all of it legal. You can also gift your own resources with gift (food, wood, ore, oil, equipment, supply or gold, paid this turn, delivered next) — a favour, a subsidy to an ally, or a bribe. You can also send your whole known map (every coordinate) with share_map; they receive it next turn in query panel=intel — useful for swapping intelligence, showing strength and coordinating offence and defence. Diplomacy costs money: every successful diplomatic act (proposal/answer/break-up/guarantee/war/peace/map swap/gift) is charged a base of {diplo} gold; letters (send_letter) are priced separately by length: **base price {ally} gold inside the alliance / {cost} gold outside** (the first {free} characters included, and the diplomatic centre discount applies: {disc} per centre, floor {floor}), **beyond that 1 gold per {per} characters (a partial {per} counts as {per}) and no discount applies** — alliance members are no longer free, a long letter still costs; proposals of alliance/bloc/peace made to you are forever free — a diplomatic power with centres has that edge. Information war: if you would rather not ask (too lazy to talk, unwilling to owe) and your treasury is deep, spy costs {spy} gold against another state and returns {spy_turns} turns later its treasury/income/full build-out, a rough read of its military (counts per unit kind only, positions unknown) and its whole known map (the map itself shows in query panel=intel); ⚠ spies **give counts only** — enemy positions, HP and designations are not readable, so dispositions and movements come only from map swaps, border watching or fighting them outright — enough to know who to hit, whom to lean on and when to open a war.
msg.ai.rules.economy: National accounts: treasury/wood/food, ore, oil, equipment, supply all sit on your books (res panel). The grid is national and stores nothing: power plants generate it; Supply Depots/Arsenals/Barracks/Town Halls all burn power to keep running, and if generation < upkeep every one of those advanced buildings stops (power plants excepted). Supply Depot({sup_in}→{sup_out}); Arsenal({eq_in}→{eq_out}); the supply depot costs {inf_sup} per army per turn (cavalry {cav_sup}), and once it is empty every army bleeds HP in proportion to its shortfall (-{starve} HP at full shortfall, still charged mid-battle) — they can starve to death. Exception: militia standing on their own garrison farm eat nothing (each farm covers 1 unit on its tile); move off and they do. Gold Mines are steady bullion; the Town Hall (needs ≥{need} used local slots · {limit} per tile · {en} power) pays {base} gold base + {per} gold per building on the tile each turn (itself excluded — the fuller the tile, the better it earns) into the treasury; you can also sell goods on the world market (dump more, get a lower price).
msg.ai.rules.mail: send_letter writes to any other state (alliance invitations, peace talks, threats, intelligence swaps), **priced by length: base price {ally} gold inside the alliance / {cost} gold outside (the first {free} characters included, diplomatic centre discount applies), then 1 gold per {per} characters with no discount at all; charged as soon as it goes, delivered next turn** — alliance members are no longer free, a long letter still costs. **Do the maths before you send: is it worth it?** Write only when the expected return (tribute you can shake down, the safety an alliance buys, intelligence you need, a forced peace that stops the bleeding) is clearly above the price; if you cannot say what it buys, don't send it — **a long letter is money spent**. Check query panel=res for the treasury first: **when the treasury is tight, don't write**; if it can ride along with a formal diplomatic proposal (the diplomatic fee) don't send a separate letter, and never use letters to chat. Answers belong in the diplomacy/mail panel — go silent and they will assume you refused.
msg.ai.rules.market: World market buy/sell: gold is the currency; food/wood/ore/oil/equipment/supply are tradeable. Supply and demand move prices: buying pushes them up, selling pushes them down; a fill settles at the **curve average** along the trade (not the worst marginal price for the whole lot), plus a {spread} buy/sell spread (buy +{half} / sell −{half}). Each turn prices drift back toward the supply/demand equilibrium — if the world produces more it gets cheaper, wartime consumption makes it dearer (the panel shows the equilibrium price). Depth is banded by good (food and wood deep, equipment shallow) and scales with the number of surviving states: the more states, the smaller a single order's impact. Base prices: {base}. Selling in instalments beats dumping the lot at once; food and wood are domestic demand (cheap, bulk), ore, oil and equipment are the export trade.
msg.ai.rules.overview: EU4-style grand-map war: everyone starts from {n} tiles — clear wilds, build, produce, field armies, and you may ally with or wage war on others. Turn based: each turn you act (as many things as you like) → then the turn resolves in one sweep (output/grid/combat/supply/market reversion). Tile names are their IDs and coordinates are 1-based. You see your own land plus the ring of tiles around it (with an alliance you also see your allies' land; watchtowers push event vision further out); other states' strength you can only guess. The fog limits what you **see**, not what you **order**: you may issue mv/atk at tiles outside your vision — when you hit an opaque wall (neutral territory, a hidden enemy, someone else's battle) the error tells you truthfully what you hit (that is what recon buys you), but the price is that the formation's movement budget for this turn is spent; hitting a wall on a tile you can see costs nothing (trial and error is free). Spare the budget and don't push blind; recon by force and accept that it cannot move this turn. For any mechanism in detail, call rules with a topic, e.g. rules(Buildings) rules(Alliance) rules(Army).
msg.ai.rules.report: Every {every} turns each state's economic report is settled **automatically** (from turns {t1}/{t2}/{t3}… onward); **on the turn it is issued (turns {t1}/{t2}/{t3}…) the full text goes into your status panel 【Economic report】**, other turns keep only a one-line summary; earlier periods and cross-period trends are the report tool's job (free, read-only) — **it cannot be run by hand** and a missed period cannot be redone. A period covers the last {every} turns, everything valued at the prices of the moment: ①GDP (this turn) = the value added produced **in the closing turn** (market prices, **excluding military spending**: extraction/factory output + gold mines/town hall gold − intermediate inputs − energy fuel) — not divided by days, not accumulated over the period, it is the current output rate; ②GDP growth = versus the previous period's closing value (two run-rates compared directly, unaffected by how long the first window happened to be); ③fiscal revenue = GDP − military spending; ④military spending (this turn) = the supply armies **actually consumed** in the closing turn × current prices (source-blind: home-produced and bought count the same); ⑤military spending as a share of GDP; ⑥national assets = replacement cost of every building (build gold + wood × current price, land taken from others included); ⑦asset growth; ⑧investment this period = what building actually cost (gold + wood × then-current prices, castle upgrades included); ⑨investment growth; ⑩foreign/domestic share = (buy+sell volume)/(own output+imports) versus the home-consumed part. report all=true for the cross-period trend table; report turn={t1} for one period. Military spending cuts both ways: too high and it squeezes investment so you fall behind over the long run; too low and you are a lamb waiting for the knife, with your room to grow held hostage.
msg.ai.rules.terrain.prose: Land is always taken with atk: send an army into a tile — if it is guarded you occupy it by winning, if there are no enemies you occupy it by walking in; mv only moves, it never claims; there is no『claim wilds out of thin air』command. Marching does not fight savages: mv may head straight into the wilds (including tiles a savage holds) and pass through — savages never attack on their own, they do not strike a column passing by, and they only engage when they are atk'd; but while a wild tile has an enemy army on it (including one mid-raid) mv is forbidden — you must atk and fight.
msg.ai.rules.turn: end_turn closes your turn. Each turn's settlement will: land pending buildings → output/grid → war → supply/healing → repatriation → market reversion. The save is written to mp_save.json every turn, so a game can be interrupted and resumed at any time. National plan: set or revise it with plan (it lives in the standing context 【National plan】); with no plan, or once {plan} turns have passed since the last revision, end_turn is blocked — plan first, then close. A good plan covers economic development, military planning, intelligence management and diplomatic direction.
msg.ai.schema.accept_peace.desc: Accept the other side's peace offer (proposal ids are in the diplomacy panel; only the named party — its negotiator — can accept; the diplomatic fee is charged on success). ⚠ If you are the chief, accepting first starts a bloc vote and only takes effect with a majority.
msg.ai.schema.attack.desc: Charge an army into the target tile (within reach for its kind: {reach}) and engage — beat the guard and the tile is yours; if there is **no army at all** on the tile you occupy it outright; so do you when a wild tile holds only neutral/allied peaceful garrisons (they do not join the fight and are repatriated at the end of the turn); a foreign tile holding a non-hostile army cannot be entered. **Don't steal someone else's battle**: if a party neither your enemy nor your ally is raiding a wild tile → you cannot atk into it (mv to watch is fine); an enemy or an ally is raiding → you may join (several parties on one tile each fight their own enemies; you only fight each other once war is declared). Occupation follows the order of claim: whoever atk'd first, then the earliest-arrived ally if it dies. Fighting another state requires a declaration of war.
msg.ai.schema.attack.p_ids: Array of your participating army ids (numbered per country from 1)
msg.ai.schema.bloc_dissolve.desc: 【chief only】Dissolve your alliance: every member returns to sovereignty (each becomes an entity again), treaties are void and bloc votes in flight are cancelled. **No dissolving during war** (refused while any member is fighting — make peace first). A chief cannot resign from a bloc: to get out, dissolve it or hand over the chair. Free.
msg.ai.schema.bloc_found.desc: Propose an alliance (a multi-party bloc): **you must name it** (1~{maxlen} characters, no spaces, unique worldwide) and invite the founding members. The alliance forms once every founding member answers with respond_proposal (any refusal kills it) and **the proposer becomes chief**. ★ The alliance is itself a **diplomatic entity**: from then on guarantees, joint defence, war and peace all go out in its name and **must pass a bloc vote**; no member signs a treaty alone. **Joining gives up personal treaties** (members' existing guarantees/joint defences are void). Inside the bloc: open borders, non-aggression, shared vision; core land is returned automatically by allies on the same front. **No founding alliances during war.** Proposing costs the diplomatic fee (base {diplo} gold; free when the invitees hold diplomatic centres).
msg.ai.schema.bloc_found.p_tos: Array of founding member states (at least 1, and they must be states from countries)
msg.ai.schema.bloc_join.desc: Apply to join a named alliance: the current members vote and **more yes than no** admits you (a chief voting no vetoes); one state belongs to at most one alliance; you cannot apply while at war with a member of that bloc, or while you are fighting at all. Costs the diplomatic fee (base {diplo} gold).
msg.ai.schema.bloc_leave.desc: Leave your alliance: an ordinary member may do so unilaterally and immediately (armies stranded on former allies' land are repatriated at the end of the turn). ★ **No leaving during war** — if any member is fighting the request is refused; members are locked in during a war, make peace first. **The chief cannot leave** — bloc_transfer the chair first, or bloc_dissolve. Costs the diplomatic fee (base {diplo} gold).
msg.ai.schema.bloc_rename.desc: 【chief only】Rename your alliance (1~{maxlen} characters, no spaces, unique worldwide). Free.
msg.ai.schema.bloc_transfer.desc: 【chief only】Hand the chair to another member of your alliance (afterwards you are an ordinary member and may leave freely). The chair belongs to the founder by default, and only the sitting chief can transfer it. Free.
msg.ai.schema.bloc_transfer.p_to: Member state that takes the chair (must be a current member)
msg.ai.schema.break_defense.desc: Lift a joint defence. ★ **No lifting during war** (treaties are frozen in wartime: neither concluding nor lifting — only peace stops the fighting) — the old 'break the treaty and you leave the front it dragged you into' was an escape hatch from a losing war, and it is closed. If you are in an alliance this first becomes a **bloc vote**, and after it passes the alliance lifts it (members cannot rescind anything alone); as a sovereign state you lift it directly. Lifting also lifts the follower status, and armies stranded on the other side's land are repatriated at the end of the turn.
msg.ai.schema.build.desc: Build one structure on one of your tiles. 1 build order per tile per turn. Buildings: {buildings}. Extractive buildings are capped by the local resource; Supply Depots/Arsenals/energy plants build anywhere (industry does not care about the site); Barracks need ≥{barracks_need} used slots on the local tile; Watchtower = event vision + a {tower_r} ring; Town Hall needs ≥{th_need} used local slots and {th_limit} per tile; Diplomatic Center halves the diplomatic cost, stacks, but only {dip_limit} may be self-built nationwide (take the 2nd by conquest); Engineers = local build cost -{academy_disc}% and needs ≥{academy_need} local slots; Garrison Farm = a **foodless** militia establishment, it raises militia ({militia_cost} per unit, nationwide militia <= garrison farms) and militia on its own tile eat no supply (needs ≥1 local {camp_res}, {camp_limit} per tile).
msg.ai.schema.build.p_tile: Tile: coordinates like '5 6' or the name of one of your tiles (see the land panel)
msg.ai.schema.buy.desc: Buy goods on the world market for gold. Buying pushes the price up; a fill settles at the **curve average** and includes a {spread} buy premium — the more urgent the bid, the more you pay (trial prices: query panel=market).
msg.ai.schema.cancel_guarantee.desc: Withdraw an independence guarantee. ★ **No withdrawals during war** (treaties are frozen in wartime, same rule as break_defense). If you are in an alliance this first becomes a bloc vote, and after it passes the alliance withdraws it.
msg.ai.schema.countries.desc: Lists every diplomatic target (every state but you: relations, whether you border them, whether they wrote to you). Pick a target with it before acting, then act with to=<that state>; you may never point a diplomatic tool at yourself.
msg.ai.schema.declare_war.desc: Declare war on another state (they must answer, effective at once; the diplomatic fee is charged on success). Pick the target with countries first and pass to=<another state> (never yourself). ★ **The belligerents are diplomatic entities**: if you are in an alliance the call becomes a **bloc war vote** (a majority brings the whole bloc in, the chief leads the attack); as a sovereign state you simply start the war. War transmission (unlimited hops, counted per entity): the target's guarantors, joint-defence partners and its alliance enter against you through the transitive closure (A guarantees B, B allies C → hit B and C comes too). If the target is already fighting an ally/partner of your entity, your declaration **merges into their existing front** as a follower (a follower cannot make separate peace; when the leader does, the whole front stops).
msg.ai.schema.econ.desc: Build-vs-buy returns at current prices: a building's cost (gold-equivalent)/margin per turn/payback time; with no building it prints the whole building economy table. Run the numbers before you build or trade.
msg.ai.schema.econ.p_building: Building to cost out (optional; omit for the whole table)
msg.ai.schema.end_turn.desc: End your actions for this turn. ⚠ summary is required: one sentence saying what you did this turn and where you stand (e.g. summary=this turn built two farms and keeps expanding). Without that line the turn is not considered ended.
msg.ai.schema.gift.desc: Send part of your own stocks to another state (to = a state from countries, never yourself): good={goods} or gold, qty = amount. Debited this turn, delivered next; a diplomatic handling fee also applies (base {diplo} gold; halved by a diplomatic centre; free when the recipient is in the same alliance). Useful for a favour, subsidising an ally, or buying loyalty.
msg.ai.schema.guarantee.desc: Guarantee another state's (entity's) independence: anyone who attacks it brings your entity into the war automatically. **Signatories are diplomatic entities**: if you are in an alliance the call first becomes a **bloc vote**, and after it passes the **alliance** extends the guarantee (the credit and the obligation belong to the bloc); as a sovereign state you are an entity yourself and it applies at once. Guarantee and joint defence are mutually exclusive (joint defence is the stronger bond and taking it cancels the guarantee). **Both entities must be at peace** (if either side is fighting, no guarantee — make peace first). to = another state (never yourself). Charged on success (base {diplo} gold).
msg.ai.schema.memory_search.desc: Search your own past memory (the **body** of actions, letters and results only — never your reasoning): keywords find the relevant turns and return **the turn number plus its neighbours**. Good for holding history against someone — 'what did I promise Chu', 'which battles burned the most supply', 'who declared war on me'. Separate keywords with spaces (e.g. pact Chu); records matching every keyword come first, partial matches after; limit caps how many are returned. Only your own memory is searchable, and nobody else is affected. Free, read-only.
msg.ai.schema.memory_search.p_query: Search keywords (several words separated by spaces)
msg.ai.schema.move.desc: Reposition one of your own armies; a pure move claims nothing. Once per army per turn. {rule} **Marching does not fight savages**: a legal move target is one of three — **a wild tile (unowned), your own tile, an ally's tile** — wilds may be entered and crossed freely (savages never attack a column passing by, they only engage when atk'd); you may also mv onto your own/allied tile held by a mixed-battle enemy (reinforcing joins the fight on arrival). **Enemy soil may never be entered by mv (empty tiles included)**: every step into their border is an atk — you either engage or walk straight in. **Nor may you mv onto a wild tile holding an enemy army you are fighting (including one mid-raid)** — that needs an atk; a wild tile held by a neutral/allied garrison may be mv'd into (stand and watch, no interference). You cannot move while in contact — retreat out first.
msg.ai.schema.offer_peace.desc: Offer peace to the other side's negotiator (each side's negotiator is its leader; if the leader is in an alliance, its chief; ordinary members and followers cannot negotiate — to = the negotiator shown in the diplomacy panel; the diplomatic fee is charged on success). ⚠ A chief's offer first starts a bloc vote and is only sent if a majority agrees. pay = we indemnify them X gold; demand = we claim X gold from them; white = white peace. Acceptance stops the whole front (followers included) and recomputes each side's core land from what they actually hold. truce = truce length in turns (0 = no truce). ★ During a war members **cannot leave or dissolve the bloc**; making peace is the only way out.
msg.ai.schema.offer_peace.p_kind: pay = we indemnify / demand = we claim indemnity / white = white peace
msg.ai.schema.offer_peace.p_truce: Truce length in turns (yours to propose, 0 = no truce)
msg.ai.schema.p_army_id: Your army id (numbered per country from 1; take it from the query army panel)
msg.ai.schema.plan.desc: Set or revise your national plan (long-term strategic goals); it stays in your context permanently under the 【National plan】 marker until you revise it. ⚠ You must have a plan before end_turn, and it must be revised every {every} turns or end_turn is blocked. Suggested four headings: economic development (food/wood/ore/oil, building, trade), military planning (expansion, offence/defence, alliances), intelligence management (spies, map swaps, reading incoming letters) and diplomatic direction (alliances, war, peace, gifts).
msg.ai.schema.propose.desc: Propose a 『joint defence』 (defensive only: if they are attacked you join automatically; your own wars do not drag them in). **Signatories are diplomatic entities**, and it matters whether your alliance or you as a sovereign state are the one signing: if you are in an alliance the call first becomes a **bloc vote** and the alliance then proposes in its name; if the other side is an alliance, its acceptance also needs its own bloc vote (one vote per bloc). For a full alliance use bloc_found. to must be a state picked from countries, never yourself. **Both entities must be at peace** (if either side is fighting, no treaty — make peace first). Diplomatic fee (base {diplo} gold; free inside the same entity; free if the other side has a diplomatic centre), charged only on success.
msg.ai.schema.query.desc: Query interface: pull any of your panels any time. res=treasury and stocks / plan=national plan / land=tiles (homeland + claimable wilds) / army=armies / market=world market (current/bid/ask/equilibrium prices + bulk-order trial) / econ=building accounting (cost, margin, payback per building) / intel=map intelligence received (all coordinates) / spy=spy reports (their economy and a rough read of their army) / mail=inbox / countries=diplomatic targets / diplomacy=diplomacy / news=recent reports / threats=enemy armies in vision / all=everything. State changes after every action, so query again when you are unsure.
msg.ai.schema.recruit.desc: Recruit on tiles you own that hold a Barracks with the grid up; each Barracks trains 1 army per turn. Unit kinds: {rows} — militia are cheap garrison troops, 1 per Garrison Farm per turn and nationwide militia <= nationwide garrison farms (refit only after a loss). Keep the supply depot ahead of you: on a shortfall every army bleeds HP in proportion to the gap (-{starve} HP/army/turn, even mid-battle), and the starved do not come back.
msg.ai.schema.recruit.militia: ; standing on its own garrison farm costs no supply
msg.ai.schema.recruit.p_kind: Unit kind (default is infantry; militia can only be raised on your own garrison farm tiles)
msg.ai.schema.reject_peace.desc: Reject the other side's peace offer and keep fighting (the diplomatic fee is charged on success).
msg.ai.schema.report.desc: Read your nation's economic report (free, read-only). A period closes **automatically** every {every} turns and can be read from the start of turns {t1}/{t2}/{t3}… — **it cannot be run by hand**. Contents: market-priced GDP and its growth, fiscal revenue net of military spending, military spending as a share of GDP, national assets and their growth, total investment this period and its growth, foreign/domestic trade share. No argument = the latest period; turn=<report turn> (e.g. {t1}); all=true = the cross-period trend table.
msg.ai.schema.report.p_all: true = the trend table across all periods
msg.ai.schema.report.p_turn: Report turn ({t1}/{t2}/{t3}…); omit = the latest period
msg.ai.schema.respond_proposal.desc: Answer an invitation you received (joint defence/alliance: accept=true to agree / false to refuse; a founding bloc only forms when everyone accepts; free inside the same entity). ★ While you are **in an alliance** a joint-defence invitation is not yours to settle: accepting merely **puts it to a bloc vote** (then state your position with vote, and more yes than no concludes it); refusing is done by the chief on behalf of the entity.
msg.ai.schema.retreat.desc: Pull an army out of contact (defenders' guards included) — **always exactly {rng} adjacent tile** (for everyone: not per unit speed, and terrain cost is ignored). Retreat does not settle at once: the army stays on the battlefield for this turn's combat settlement (damage is spread across the field; a retreating defender keeps {cover}% of its reduction and outputs -{pen}% this turn) and disengages to the target tile afterwards. Legal targets: your own/allied/unowned wild tiles; with no legal spot around you, you cannot retreat. mv cannot leave a contact tile — to leave a battlefield use retreat.
msg.ai.schema.rules.desc: Read the full game rules: building costs and caps, terrain, the grid economy, army and combat, diplomacy, mail, the market, turns and saving. Pass a topic to get only the relevant sections (e.g. 'barracks', 'diplomacy', 'war'); with no topic you get everything.
msg.ai.schema.sell.desc: Sell goods to the world market for gold. Selling pushes the price down; a fill settles at the **curve average** minus a {spread} sell spread, and a big order slaps its own price down (trial prices: query panel=market) — instalments beat a dump.
msg.ai.schema.send_letter.desc: Write to another state. **Priced by length: base price {ally} gold inside the alliance / {cost} gold outside (the first {free} characters included, diplomatic centre discount applies: {disc} per centre, floor {floor}); every {per} characters past {free} costs 1 gold with no discount at all**. Charged as soon as it goes, delivered next turn; alliance members are no longer free. A long letter is money spent — do the maths first: is it worth it? Write only when the expected return (tribute/alliance/intelligence/a forced peace) clearly beats the price; if you cannot say what it buys, don't write, and never use letters to chat. When the treasury is tight, keep it short or skip it. If the ask can ride along with a formal diplomatic proposal (the diplomatic fee), don't send a separate letter. to must be a state from countries, never yourself.
msg.ai.schema.share_map.desc: Send your whole known map (every tile you own plus the visible ring beyond the border, with coordinates) to another state; they receive it next turn in query panel=intel (diplomatic fee, base {diplo} gold, charged only on success; free when the target is in the same alliance). Good for swapping intelligence, showing your hand or synchronising campaigns. to = a state from countries, never yourself.
msg.ai.schema.spy.desc: When you would rather not ask (too lazy to talk, deep pockets), send a spy: {cost} gold (refused if the treasury cannot cover it), and {turns} turns later you get the state's full economic picture (query panel=spy — treasury/stocks, last turn's income, the buildings and pending work on every tile)**, a rough read of its army (counts per unit kind only; positions, HP and designations do not leak)**, plus its whole known map (in query panel=intel). You cannot spy on yourself.
msg.ai.schema.vote.desc: State your position in a bloc vote in progress (war/peace/join/pact). choice=yes for / no against / abstain (not voting counts as abstention at the deadline). **More yes than no passes it** (abstentions are not in the denominator) and it executes at once; **a chief voting no is a veto and voids the motion immediately**. Votes may be changed; voting is free for bloc members. ★ The pact vote is this game's **only** treaty channel: guarantees and joint defences can only be signed or lifted this way.
msg.ai.text.move_cost: each tile you step on is charged by terrain (the dearer of the tile you leave and the tile you enter): Cavalry is cheap on {fast} but costs double on {slow} (⇒ only {n} tiles, and **it cannot break through**); {kinds} pay {flat} per tile on any terrain
msg.ai.text.move_rule: **Movement**: {rows}; {cost}. A multi-tile move is **judged tile by tile**: a Mountain/Forest in the way, or borrowing a lane through someone else's land, both stop you cold.
msg.ai.tip.expand: There is no separate settle command: land is taken only through atk — send an army to attack a tile; if it holds no defenders/enemies (enemies=0) the army walks in and occupies it; if savages or enemies are there, winning takes it; a tile in the wild held only by neutral/allied peacekeepers is also occupied on entry (they do not fight and are sent home at end of turn). mv only moves, it never claims; if an enemy holds the wild tile (including one fighting savages) you must atk, not mv.
msg.ai.turn.need_plan: The turn cannot end yet: no state policy. Call plan(content=…) first (it stays in context as your long-term goal; cover economy / military / intelligence / diplomacy).
msg.ai.turn.need_summary: The turn is not closed: end_turn must carry summary=one line on what you did and where you stand (e.g. summary=two farms built this turn, keep expanding).
msg.ai.turn.stale_plan: The turn cannot end yet: your state policy has not been revised for {n} turns (it must be revised every {every} turns). Update it first with plan(content=…).
msg.ai.warn.military: ⚠ Military spending cuts both ways: too much crowds out investment and you fall behind over the long run; too little makes you a sitting target — trade it off yourself.
